paragraphs.text: Moonfolk is a creature type for cards that depict a race of humanoid beings who are capable of flight , and are native to Kamigawa . Physically, they are slim, possess blue-gray skin, and have long ears which they wrap over their heads.
Moonfolk are primarily mono- blue , though Kotori, Pilot Prodigy and Genku, Future Shaper are white-blue .

The moonfolk were conceived by Japanese artist Ittoku, who introduced the subtle rabbit-like elements (white hair, long ears, and so on). The type took inspiration from both the Moon Rabbit and Lady Kaguya from Japanese mythology .

The creature type originally appeared in the Kamigawa block . At this time, all Moonfolk were mono- blue and had activations that required bouncing your lands. R&D (mostly) stopped doing that on the return as it wasn’t great gameplay.
The planeswalker Tamiyo was the only Moonfolk to have appeared outside of the Kamigawa block until Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty (a period of 17 years).

The Moonfolk or Soratami (soh-rah-TAH-mee; Japanese: 空 民 ; literally: "Skyfolk") are an enigmatic race of humanoid beings who mainly dwell in Kamigawa 's clouds. They claim to be descended from a moon Myojin . The Moonfolk live within floating palaces in the clouds, particularly in the flying city of Otawara . They watch over the world below, mostly indifferent to the concerns of the surface folk. They have a high emphasis on the study of magic and have some of the most learned mages on the plane.

During the Kami War era, Mochi and the soratami secretly worked together in a plan to make the soratami the dominant species on Kamigawa by manipulating Konda into inciting a war between mortals and kami. However, these efforts would ultimately fail.

By the Kamigawa's Modern Age , the Moonfolk seem to have warmed slightly to the other mortal races of Kamigawa, opening Otawara to outsiders (though still not Oboro palace itself), and allowing the city to become a center of innovation.

Ages later, the Moonfolk opened up Otawara to the other mortal races (though still not Oboro palace itself), and established the Saiba Futurists . Revolutionary techniques developed by the Futurists became one of the two important innovations in establishing Kamigawa's Modern Age , and allowed Otawara to become the plane's new center of learning and innovation. With their rising success, the moonfolk asked the dragon kami Kairi to protect their city, only for the great kami to refuse. The Soratami still make up a majority of the Saiba Futurists and have produced many of the plane's most revolutionary artificers .
